Sus reflexiones sobre dónde se está generando el valor a largo plazo, y qué se necesita para asegurarlo, les dieron a todos los presentes mucho en qué actuar.

¡Y gracias a todas las personas que nos acompañaron! Es a través de conversaciones como esta que el mercado avanza en materia de calidad.

posts.content:
On 21 September, as part of New York Climate Week, I am hosting a conversation about the new era of corporate decarbonisation, the options and what we are seeing in the market.

Cut at source. Inset inside your value chain. Buy lower-carbon physical supply. Use mass balance. Buy environmental attribute certificates. Buy carbon credits.

Each has a different cost per tonne and a different accounting treatment, but they all come from the same strategy and the same budget.

The rules evolved this summer - SBTi published Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2 in June. GHG Protocol announced in July that it will consolidate its corporate standards with ISO into a single co-branded standard. ISO is still in draft, with publication expected next year. Between them, they have started to build the architecture for market-based instruments, but the consolidated GHGP/ISO standard is not due until 2028. Meanwhile, offtakes are being signed this year for delivery in 2028 and beyond, against rules that are still evolving.

We will discuss what each lever does to a reported number, how buyers are actually sequencing them and what we are seeing across the value chain and wider market.

I am looking forward to this event and moderating the session, mostly because of the fantastic lineup of speakers who cover roles across the market:

Sam Israelit, Partner and Chief Sustainability Officer, Bain & Company
Yuhau Lin, VP Environmental Commodities, Morgan Stanley
Bernhard Stormyr, VP Sustainability Governance, Yara International
Allister Furey, CEO and co-founder, Sylvera

We have seen extremely high interest in this event, so we are currently operating a waiting list, but I am in New York all week. If you are a buyer reviewing your decarbonisation strategy, looking for lower-carbon commodities or EACs, or a producer looking to sell your lower-carbon product, from cement and steel to ammonia and fertiliser, please send me a message, and it would be great to grab a coffee.

posts.content:
A Letter of Authorization signals a country's intent to apply corresponding adjustments. But it's the years of reporting that follow that actually make an ITMO credible. 

In an Article 6 & CORSIA Hub exclusive deep-dive, our International Policy Lead Carmen Álvarez Campo looks at what the first wave of real-world Article 6.2 submissions shows.

Reporting gaps fall into three categories: timeliness, completeness, and accuracy. And all three are already appearing in early filings. 

Even LDCs and SIDS, who get flexibility on deadlines, aren't exempt from the risk. Without an up-to-date GHG inventory, corresponding adjustments can't be reliably applied.

The stakes differ by who's holding the credit:

🛬 CORSIA-compliant airlines face indirect exposure through unit integrity, while sovereign buyers carry the risk directly against their own NDC targets

🤝 Investors and developers may find authorizations that look solid on paper but can't be substantiated when reporting falls short

☑️ Insurers are starting to price host-country reporting quality into how they underwrite carbon credit delivery risk

With CORSIA Phase 1 compliance approaching and 2030 NDC deadlines closing in, reporting quality is quickly becoming a frontline due diligence issue rather than a technicality.

Read Carmen's full breakdown - including the complete reporting timeline and what "good" looks like going forward - on the Sylvera Article 6 & CORSIA Hub: https://lnkd.in/eAaHzrHc

posts.content:
Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) reduces methane emissions and water consumption through sustainable rice farming, without compromising yields. 

Carbon markets are increasingly funding superpollutant project types - such as AWD - to reduce and avoid emissions like methane. And buyers need a reliable way to assess which projects are delivering the impact they claim.

We've launched our new Alternate Wetting & Drying (AWD) Ratings Framework, bringing the same rigour we apply across all of Sylvera's ratings to this growing project type. It covers:

💧 Carbon Accounting: are water levels and methane fluxes accurately monitored, are baseline assumptions and emission factors applied conservatively?

 💧 Additionality: is AWD already common practice or policy-mandated in the region, and would these farmers have adopted it without carbon finance?

 💧 Permanence: is there any risk of reversal?

 💧 Co-benefits: does the project deliver on water savings, farmer livelihoods, and community impact?

posts.content:
Today is Earth Overshoot Day, the day humanity's used up what nature can regenerate this year.

We’re launching the Open Carbon Data Project with support from The Rockefeller Foundation, Meta, World Resources Institute, Symbiosis Coalition, and researchers at the Universidade Estadual de Santa Cruz (UESC) in Bahia, Brazil.

What does it mean? Our teams are out in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest combining some of the most advanced forest-measurement tech available: terrestrial and airborne laser scanning, gamma spectrometry, with on-the-ground verification. This is the same kind of ground-truth data that feeds into Meta and WRI's AI-powered Canopy Height Maps, one of the most widely used forest monitoring tools in the world. 

Better ground data means sharper AI models, and sharper models mean carbon numbers people can actually trust.

Later this year, we're releasing all of it free, open licence, with no string - so anyone building monitoring tools, developing new projects, running a registry, or investing in this space can use it. The people we think about most are the smallholders and community-led projects in Bahia who've done the work of protecting these forests for years, and who deserve a market that can actually see and reward that.

Proud to be doing this alongside partners who care as much about scaling investments for forest restoration and protection as we do.

More on the dataset as it's released: https://lnkd.in/dfVyg7r2

posts.content:
A lot has shifted in carbon markets policy in recent weeks. SBTi V2.0, ISO 14060, EU ETS developments. 

Our policy team has been working through the detail across all of it. 

The consistent thread across the board: quality has become the price of entry.
In this article, we analyse how SBTi and ISO converge on their requirements for carbon credits:

✅ Additional
✅ Independently verified
✅ Separately accounted
✅ No double counting
✅ Project-level due diligence required

ISO goes one step further, explicitly naming ratings agencies as a benchmark for assessing whether a removal meets its quality bar.

For buyers, the diligence need is rising. For producers, integrity will determine access to a new wave of standards-aligned demand.

See our ISO - SBTi analysis here: https://lnkd.in/eyNyu8WP

posts.content:
The European Commission has today published its proposed overhaul of the EU Emissions Trading System - the policy that will shape Europe's carbon market through 2040.

Our policy experts Carmen Álvarez Campo and Ben Rattenbury have broken down what each of these means for buyers, developers, and investors in carbon markets.

Key takeaways:

🛫 CORSIA: no major demand shock. The expected "ETS grab" of international flights didn't happen. Only routes within 5,000km of the EU (think Doha, Istanbul, Dubai) shift into the ETS from 2029. Eligibility criteria for CORSIA units are also being loosened.

🍃  Removals: a door has opened, but a narrow one. A 250 MtCO2e allowance (with a +10Mt cushion if that's not enough) will be increased and auctioned to allow the purchase of up to an equal amount of permanent removals (DAC, BECCS certified under the EU CRCF) into the ETS from 2031–2040, but only via a new centralized EU body.

🌍 Article 6 credits: up to 260M credits (2036–40) financed with an equal amount of allowances. A 2031–35 pilot phase comes first, with eligibility and quality criteria yet to be defined.

📉 The Linear Reduction Factor: holds at 4.4% through 2028-2030, then eases to 3.7% (2031–35) and 1.7% (2036–40) — a deliberate softening of the path to 2040. (edited)

🏭 Free allowances: reframed as "investment allowances," tied to companies actually delivering on decarbonisation plans. CBAM-exposed sectors keep free allocation until 2038.

Abandoned oil and gas wells leak methane - one of the most potent greenhouse gases on the planet. Without ownership to seal them, they can leak for decades.

Carbon markets are stepping in to fill the funding gap. And buyers need a reliable way to assess which projects are delivering the impact they claim.

We've launched our new Orphan Oil & Gas (OOG) Well Ratings Framework, bringing the same rigour we apply across all of Sylvera's ratings to this fast-growing project type. It covers:

🔩 Carbon Accounting: are pre-plugging emissions accurately measured, and are terminal decline rates and GWP values applied conservatively?
 🔩 Additionality: is government funding genuinely insufficient, and would these wells have been plugged without carbon finance?
 🔩 Permanence: is the plugging built to last, and is there a risk of methane migrating to nearby unplugged wells?
 🔩 Co-benefits: does the project deliver on air quality, groundwater protection, and community impact?

posts.content:
📊 Our latest carbon market analysis is here 📊

Some key themes in the data:

1️⃣ Volume down, value up. Retirements fell 10% YoY to 38.55M, but total market value rose to $247M as average price per credit climbed to $6.41 (from $5.29).

2️⃣ The offtake market is diversifying. Microsoft's pullback (-82%) was the big offtake story of H1, but new names are stepping up, with the second-largest offtaker in H1 2026 announcing double 2025's runner-up volume. Biochar saw strong growth, and non-Microsoft ARR volume nearly tripled.

3️⃣ Quality pricing gap continues to widen. REDD+'s quality spread has nearly tripled since Q2 2025, and IFM's premium has grown to over $5.50/tonne in a year.

4️⃣ Cookstoves are holding strong, drawing level with REDD+ as the largest retirement category for the first time, up from 4th place last quarter.

5️⃣ CORSIA compliance demand is showing up. 502k CORSIA credits were retired in H1 2026, up from just 14k in all of 2025. But supply is tight — only 38M credits meet full EEU eligibility today, against a base-case demand of 163M by January 2028.

6️⃣ Corporate demand could be about to shift structurally. SBTi-aligned companies are currently offsetting just 0.06% of emissions, against a 1% minimum threshold under the new Corporate Net-Zero Standard.
